difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes derived completeness of an object with respect to an ideal, in the Koszul setup of the section, as the property that the object is isomorphic to the derived limit of its tensor products with the Koszul system (statement lines 26341-26350, formulated inside the situation of the section). One implication is a previous statement, while the converse filters the Koszul complexes by stupid truncations, uses exactness of the derived limit construction in the second variable to reduce to the graded pieces, and then identifies the derived limits of the graded pieces with direct sums of torsion functors, which vanish by assumption (proof lines 26352-26384). The filtration and the explicit computation of the graded pieces are the substance of the argument. The counted statement depends on the situation of the section, which is delivered as the context span, and the counted span refers four times, of which three are carried as navigation stubs.
